thread:
Anya: Heads up — CI canary failed on the eval runner, holdout fingerprint changed after a dataset regen. Did we rotate fixtures without updating the fingerprint whitelist?
Matt: Reproduced locally. eval-runner shows ~3k mismatches but most diffs look like ordering/meta only, not semantic.
Lucas: That sounds like the synthetic prompt generator changed sampling order in the last patch. We hash the prompt list as-is for the fingerprint.
Sara: Which commit? I pushed RNG reseed fixes yesterday. Could be that.
Anya: eval-bot posted the canary result: 

eval-bot: Canary run 2033456789: holdout coverage dropped from 0.020 -> 0.010 (threshold 0.015). Failing tests: holdout_integrity, promptset_fingerprint_check. Logs: https://ci.internal/runs/2033456789/log

Matt: quick diff of fixtures shows identical items but different ordering and a couple of metadata keys shuffled (source_id, timestamp). The fingerprinter concatenates prompt + metadata then sha256.
Lucas: Minimal fix is to make fingerprinting deterministic: sort prompts by stable key before hashing or canonicalize JSON. Quick example: 

```
def fingerprint(prompts):
    # canonical, order-insensitive fingerprint
    return sha256("\n".join(sorted(map(json.dumps, prompts))).encode()).hexdigest()
```

Sara: Sorting will hide intentional ordering bugs (some workloads rely on prompt order). Maybe keep two fingerprints: content_hash (order-insensitive) and order_hash (order-sensitive). CI should gate on content_hash for holdout leakage, and optionally on order_hash for ordering regressions.
Anya: Agree. For unblock we should change the canary check to accept content_hash and only fail if content_hash changes and the diff is semantically different.
Matt: I'll open a small patch to compute both hashes and update the fingerprint check. Also will add a unit test that reorders a fixture and ensures content_hash stays same.
ci-bot: Created PR #4321:fix/fingerprint-canonicalize targeting main (author: Matt). CI: running tests.
Lucas: FYI, downstream quant branch also has the old fingerprint code. Matt, can you cherry-pick?
Matt: Yep, will cherry-pick to quant-ops branch after main merges.
Anya: I'll update the holdout_whitelist with the new canonical fingerprints for the canary that already ran so it doesn't block other PRs.
Sara: Also worth adding a small doc in the eval-harness README about fingerprint semantics (content vs order) and how to regenerate golden fixtures.
Anya: Good call. I'll draft the doc and link from the PR. For now merging the canonical-sort patch should unblock CI. @Matt please leave a note in the PR about potential hidden ordering regressions so we track them.
Matt: Done. :thumbsup:
Lucas: Also adding a tiny canary that runs synthetic-generator at a fixed seed to detect accidental reseeds in future.
Anya: Perfect. Closing loop: patch + whitelist update + doc + cherry-pick. Thanks everyone. :sparkles:
